earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists/ethnography (Hale & Tindale 1933-34; Haviland & Hart 1998); no grammar or phonology of Barrow Point exists

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page barr1247 and Glottolog sources.bib entries tagged Barrow Point [bpt] (Sutton 1979 Australian language names; Van Tiggelen 2005 newspaper feature; Hale & Tindale; Haviland & Hart 1998)
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology reference exists for Barrow Point (0 descriptive refs).

sources.citation: Hale, Herbert M. & Norman B. Tindale. 1933-34. Aborigines of Princess Charlotte Bay, North Queensland. Records of the South Australian Museum 5(1):63-116, 5(2):117-172. (LANGUAGE section pp.158-159; comparative vocabulary with a Mutumui = Barrow Point/Eibole column from p.160)
sources.note: Only a notation remark, p.158: 'A stress accent is placed at the beginning of the emphasized syllable.' In the Mutumui (Barrow Point) vocabulary column the mark is applied only sporadically and falls on different syllables (p.160: 'yorlpan, 'armun, 'workan with initial stress; walan'gar, awul'war with non-initial stress; most words unmarked). No rule for where stress falls is stated.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. Publications list and Curriculum Vitae, pages.ucsd.edu/~jhaviland (Publications/; Publications/ directory listing incl. FogBook/ and FieldNOtes/)
sources.note: Confirms Haviland published no grammar/sketch/phonology of Barrow Point: only the 1998 memoir and the 2006 lexicography chapter; CV lists fieldwork on Barrow Point language 1980-1992 ('Uwu I:bu:linnganh') and an unpublished 'Barrow Point Wordlist' (computer listings, 1982-1989). FieldNOtes/ directory holds only 1966-68 Chiapas/Suriname notes.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Barrow Point language' (wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Third-hand: says Barrow Point had fricatives /ð/ and /ɣ/ that 'usually developed from *t̪ and *k, respectively, when preceded by a stressed long vowel, which then shortened', citing Dixon 2002. No statement of synchronic stress placement.

sources.citation: Flinders, Johnny & Peter Sutton. 2025. Cardinal direction enclitics in the Flinders Island Language, Cape York Peninsula. In Projecting Voices (ANU Press), ch. 12. DOI 10.22459/PV.2025.12
sources.note: Flinders Island language only (one remark: FI maleerra 'mast' has primary stress on V2); nothing on Barrow Point.

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. 2019. Phonemic inventories of Australia (database of 392 languages): inventory 2892 'Malthanmungu' [barr1247, bpt]. In S. Moran & D. McCloy (eds), PHOIBLE 2.0. Jena: MPI-SHH. With: Round, Erich. 2019. Australian phonemic inventories contributed to PHOIBLE 2.0: Essential explanatory notes (Zenodo 3464333).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Segment inventory only: 25 phonemes (p t̪ t ʈ ȶ k, m n̪ n ɳ ȵ ŋ, l r ɻ j w; vowels i iː e eː a aː u uː), no tone entries, no fricatives listed (contrast Dixon 2002:610). Round's note: 'Inferred from lexical data in Sutton nd' (Sutton's unpublished Barrow Point wordlist in Bowern's Chirila). ER data carry no stress or tone information by design.

sources.citation: Pama Language Centre. 2018. Barrow Point Language (language-variety page, posted 17 April 2018; template fields AUSTLANG reference, phonemic transcription/phonology chart link, linguistic notes & sources, all unfilled; states that summary information 'assembled by the Cape York Peninsula Languages Survey' is available on request). Cairns: Pama Language Centre.https://www.pamacentre.org.au/barrow-point/
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: the page is an unfilled template ('This language variety currently does not receive Pama Language Centre support'); the only lead is the offer of an unpublished survey summary on request. Pointer only; not a descriptive source.

sources.citation: AIATSIS Audiovisual Archive. 2011 [last updated 20 December 2016; Internet Archive copy 5 Feb 2017]. Finding aid SUTTON_P15: Guide to sound recordings collected by Peter Sutton, 1975. Canberra: Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies. 24 pp. (Prepared October 2011 by SL.)
sources.note: Nothing. It is a 24-page archival finding aid (PDF has a text; read in full via extracted text): access conditions, scope note, a cassette list (21 cassettes, items SUTTON_P15-004913 to 004933 = field tapes C20-C40) and per-item timing-point descriptions. Barrow Point language content: 004923/C30 (35:17 'Elicitation of clan names in Barrow Point language and Flinders Island language'), 004924/C31 (clan names; 09:15 'Elicitation of terms for body parts and human classification.. in Barrow Point language and Flinders Island language with Mary Ann Mundy and Johnny Flinders'), 004927/C34, 004929/…

sources.citation: AIATSIS Audiovisual Archive. 2007 (prepared March 2007, last updated 4 January 2017). Finding aid SUTTON_P07: Sound recordings collected by Peter Sutton, 1974. Canberra: AIATSIS. 16 pp. (3 reels + 10 cassettes recorded Sept-Oct 1974 at Cooktown, Cape Melville, Clack Island, Cairns, Palm Island, Townsville with Johnny Flinders, Bob Flinders, Bill McGreen; Flinders Island language and 'Biyalgeyi'; item 003355A/C7 tagged 'Flinders Island language, Mutumui'.)
sources.note: nothing: a catalogue of recordings; no linguistic description of any kind. Its only Barrow Point-related content is the item entry quoted below. Value: tells a requester that SUTTON_P07 is NOT where Sutton's Barrow Point language tapes are (Flinders Island material only, plus one Mutumui oral-history discussion).

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 2006. Documenting lexical knowledge. In J. Gippert, N. Himmelmann & U. Mosel (eds), Essentials of Language Documentation, 129-162. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter; read in the Spanish version: Haviland, 'La documentacion del conocimiento lexico', ch. 6 of Haviland & Flores Farfan (coords.) 2007, Bases de la documentacion linguistica, Mexico: INALI (scanned text).
sources.note: Nothing. Barrow Point elicitation with Roger Hart is used as a lexicographic example (working through Guugu Yimithirr); no phonology, no transcription conventions for stress.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2001. Where have all the onsets gone? Initial consonant loss in Australian Aboriginal languages. In Simpson et al. (eds), Forty Years On: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 481-492. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 512.
sources.note: Appendix table lists 'Barrow Point Lg.' as an initial-dropping language of the 'sporadic' type, sourced to 'Alpher (1976) (pers. comm. from John Haviland via Bruce Rigsby)'; no statement about Barrow Point stress placement.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. with Roger Hart. 1998. Old Man Fog and the Last Aborigines of Barrow Point. Washington DC: Smithsonian Institution Press. (author-posted scans: Front matter/Introduction pp. xv-xviii; Afterward, Glossary, Notes, Bibliography, Index)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic memoir; Barrow Point words in bold italics, no pronunciation guide. Note 42 (p.199) remarks only that variant place-name spellings 'attest to a complex vowel system in the Barrow Point language whose proper reconstruction is probably now impossible.'

sources.citation: Ogilvie, Sarah. 1994. The Morrobalama (Umbuygamu) language of Cape York Peninsula, Australia. MA thesis, Australian National University. ANU Open Research hdl 1885/110346.
sources.note: wordlist column and cognate percentages only; the stress section (2.3, p.38: stress mostly on the vowel after the first consonant) concerns Morrobalama, not Barrow Point

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 1991. 'That was the last time I seen them, and no more': voices through time in Australian Aboriginal autobiography. American Ethnologist 18(2):331-361.
sources.note: Nothing on Barrow Point word stress; transcript conventions only (capitals for emphasis/volume in Roger Hart's English/Guugu Yimithirr narrative).

sources.citation: AIATSIS AUSTLANG entry Y63.1 'Barrow Point' (lists MS and audio holdings: Sutton 1970/1975-76 Barrow Point recordings with Roger Hart and Toby Gordon, e.g. AIATSIS Archive LA4947a; Haviland 1982/1984 AIAS-funded fieldwork deposits)
sources.note: Catalogue of the unpublished primary materials (Sutton, Haviland, Sommer) in which any stress notes would reside; page blocked (not reachable by automated download) by automated download.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 1982. Kin and country at Wakooka outstation: an exercise in rich interpretation. International Journal of the Sociology of Language 36: 53-70. (Author-posted scan and.doc, pages.ucsd.edu/~jhaviland/Publications/Wakooka/.)
sources.note: No phonology. States only that BP 'is also related to GY and has many cognate words, but is phonologically rather different'; gives a handful of glossed BP utterances (e.g. inya awudha mute.. 'It wasn't a native who killed the game') without prosodic marking.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter. 1980. Cause, origin and possession in the Flinders Island language. In Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 13, 119-143. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics A-59.
sources.note: Mentions Barrow Point only for kin-term cognates (ami / t-ami 'FF'); nothing on its stress.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter & Bruce Rigsby. 1979. Linguistic communities and social networks on Cape York Peninsula. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), Australian Linguistic Studies, 713-732. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics C-54.
sources.note: No phonology content; p.714 notes 'striking lexical and phonological differences' among the ~10 Princess Charlotte Bay languages, nothing specific to Barrow Point.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter. 2016. The Flinders Islands and Cape Melville people in history. In J.-C. Verstraete & D. Hafner (eds), Land and Language in Cape York Peninsula and the Gulf Country, 85-104. Amsterdam: John Benjamins (CLU 18).

sources.note: Sutton recorded Barrow Point language in 1970 and 1975-76; this regional chapter may summarise the linguistic varieties (Flinders Island vs Barrow Point) though it is primarily historical.

sources.citation: Dixon, R. M. W. 2002. Australian Languages: Their Nature and Development. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (ch. 12 phonology: initial-dropping and fricative sections mentioning Barrow Point, data from Haviland p.c.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only printed work known to comment on Barrow Point prosodic history (fricatives from stops after a 'stressed long vowel'); may state whether stress stayed initial or shifted after initial-dropping. Second-hand, but the best available in print.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 1980-1992. Barrow Point (Uwu I:bu:linnganh) field recordings, elicitation notes and 'Barrow Point Wordlist' (computer listings Barrow Point/English, 1982-1989), with Roger Hart; deposited AIATSIS (sound collections) / held by the author, UCSD

sources.note: The only substantial documentation of the language by a linguist; any first-hand stress observation (or audio for measurement) would be here. Unpublished.
